results.name: Dynatrace Buys US Startup Arize for $915 Million to Strengthen Its Position in the AI Race
results.content:
Dynatrace (NYSE: DT) has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Arize. The deal is valued at $915 million and, according to the company’s announcement, consists of roughly $815 million in cash plus replacement equity awards for Arize employees ...
Dynatrace (NYSE: DT) has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Arize. The deal is valued at $915 million and, according to the company’s announcement, consists of roughly $815 million in cash plus replacement equity awards for Arize employees joining Dynatrace.
For Dynatrace — founded in Linz in 2005 by Bernd Greifeneder, today headquartered in the greater Boston area and listed on the New York Stock Exchange — this is the biggest purchase the company has ever made. Previous acquisitions such as Bindplane (April 2026), Metis, Runecast or Rookout (2023) were in far smaller territory; in most cases the price was never disclosed at all. Arize was founded in 2020, is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and offers a platform that lets engineering teams test, evaluate and monitor the behaviour of machine learning models, large language models and AI agents in production — for instance to detect hallucinations, measure drops in output quality or spot data drift.
The company is also known for its open-source tool Phoenix and the developer community around it. In total, Arize had raised around $131 million in venture capital, according to Tracxn data.
With Arize, Dynatrace wants to close that gap and connect pre-release evaluation with production monitoring — including GPU utilisation and infrastructure health. “AI is now moving into production at incredible speed, and the resulting AI Observability market opportunity is enormous,” Dynatrace CEO Rick McConnell is quoted as saying in the announcement. The acquisition, he says, accelerates the roadmap and extends the company’s reach into the developer community.

results.name: Dynatrace to Acquire Arize for $915 Million, Expanding AI Observability Platform | citybiz
results.content:
Dynatrace (NYSE: DT) has agreed to acquire San Francisco-based Arize in a $915 million cash-and-stock transaction, expanding the software company’s... Read More
Dynatrace (NYSE: DT) has agreed to acquire San Francisco-based Arize in a $915 million cash-and-stock transaction, expanding the software company’s AI observability capabilities as enterprises move more generative AI applications and autonomous agents from development into production.
The consideration includes approximately $815 million in cash as well as replacement equity awards for Arize employees joining Dynatrace. Dynatrace plans to fund the transaction with cash on hand, its existing credit facility or a combination of the two. The acquisition is designed to give Dynatrace an end-to-end platform spanning the AI application lifecycle, from experimentation and pre-deployment evaluation through production monitoring and optimization. The company views AI observability as a major component of its growth strategy and estimates the market will exceed $10 billion by 2030.
Beyond monitoring whether applications and infrastructure are functioning, companies need tools to evaluate output quality, identify hallucinations, track model and agent behavior and understand the relationship between AI performance, infrastructure usage and business outcomes. Dynatrace already provides observability capabilities across applications and infrastructure. Arize extends that reach into AI development and evaluation, creating a potential bridge between the teams building AI applications and those responsible for operating them in production.
Lopatecki will continue leading the Arize team and report directly to McConnell, providing management continuity as Dynatrace integrates the technology and expands its AI product strategy. The transaction is also expected to affect Dynatrace’s near-term financial profile. The company projects the acquisition will add approximately 200 basis points to annual recurring revenue growth in fiscal 2027 while reducing its non-GAAP operating margin by approximately 175 basis points.

results.name: Arize AI - aVenture Company Research
results.content:
Arize AI is a unified AI observability and evaluation platform for developing and maintaining production AI systems.  
Arize AI provides an enterprise platform (Arize AX) and open-source offering (Arize Phoenix) for AI observability, evaluation, and agent engineering. The platform supports tracing, monitoring, prompt optimization, and automated evaluations for both traditional ML and generative AI use cases. Headquartered in Berkeley, CA, the company serves enterprises including Booking.com, PepsiCo, Uber, and TripAdvisor.  
Founded in 2020 by Jason Lopatecki and Aparna Dhinakaran, Arize AI has raised over $131 million across five funding rounds, including a $70 million Series C in February 2025 led by Adams Street Partners. The company acquired Velvet in March 2025 and maintains partnerships with Deloitte Canada, Infogain, Microsoft Azure, and AFWERX.  
Companies similar to Arize AI include [Aporia](https://aventure.vc/companies/aporia-san-jose-ca-us), [Langfuse](https://aventure.vc/companies/langfuse-berlin-de), [Arthur](https://aventure.vc/companies/arthur-washington-d-c-us) and [Parea](https://aventure.vc/companies/parea-ai-ny-us).  
Arize AI was founded in 2020.  
Arize AI's headquarters is located in Berkeley, CA, US.  
Arize AI's most recent funding round was for $70M (USD) in February 2025.  
As of Feb 20, 2025, Arize AI has raised a total of $131M (USD).  
Arize AI has 93 employees as of Feb 5, 2024.

Dynatrace is acquiring Arize, an AI observability company focused on monitoring, evaluating and tracing AI applications and agents.
The deal aims to connect Arize’s visibility into model outputs, agent trajectories and tool use with Dynatrace’s application, service and infrastructure telemetry. Bringing those data sets together could help DevOps, SRE and platform teams trace AI-related failures back through the systems and transactions involved. Dynatrace announced Thursday it has agreed to acquire AI observability company Arize in a $915 million cash and stock transaction.
Rick McConnell, CEO of Dynatrace, said the company expects demand for AI observability will keep growing as more AI systems move into production. He said acquiring Arize would speed up Dynatrace’s roadmap, expand its developer reach and bring Arize’s AI team into the company.
Dynatrace is acquiring Arize, an AI observability company focused on monitoring, evaluating and tracing AI applications and agents.
Its tools track what happens during an AI or agent run, including model calls, retrieval and tool use, and use those traces to evaluate both the final output and the path the agent took to reach it. Arize co-founder Jason Lopatecki said the company collects billions of agent trajectory events, while Dynatrace tracks what the surrounding software does.
